findings.title: [P2] Separate mirror readiness from unselected pull-cache routing
findings.body: The newly registered diagram presents Mirror → Buster/BuildKit as “current readiness and pull cache,” although only readiness is selected. At pinned commit 13bff0a18a64e74f2cbbaa1978e746fcdeff0c10, charts/kubeclaw/values.yaml:47–59 leaves registry-client endpoints empty, while :345–349 independently selects registry readiness probes. scripts/registry-client-config.mjs:57–74 adds Docker Hub routing only when an explicit mirror is supplied; my-values/infra/registry-mirror.yaml:4–7 explicitly warns that deploying the cache configures no client. The same page's dependency table correctly explains this distinction. Publishing the combined edge implies a selected BuildKit cache path that the source contradicts. Label the current edge readiness-only and represent pull caching as conditional on explicit client configuration, preserving that condition in the text alternative.

findings.title: [P2] Distinguish external storage provisioning from K3s services
findings.body: The registered graph's K3s → “CSI and StorageClasses” edge, reinforced by “K3s supplies ... storage” in its text alternative, conflates cluster services with separately supplied storage contracts. At pinned commit 13bff0a18a64e74f2cbbaa1978e746fcdeff0c10, scripts/platform-services.mjs:1–5 and :23–39 explicitly adopt an existing, independently synchronized SMB CSI chart from its own upstream repository. This is not evidence that K3s supplies that driver or a suitable StorageClass. The page itself requires an existing cluster and an operator-selected StorageClass. Represent CSI/StorageClass provisioning as an external prerequisite supporting workloads, with K3s hosting/consuming it, so readers do not infer that cluster installation satisfies retained-volume prerequisites.

overall_explanation: NOT_READY for diagram-4dc422d67c265fd9 only. The literal graph contains 20 arrows, not 23. Two source contradictions prevent semantic closeout: selected mirror routing and K3s ownership of external storage. Read-only git-show inspection of full pinned objects supports the bounded configuration relationships for Redis (charts/kubeclaw/values.yaml:226–232), managed reasoning (:210–213), LiteLLM → Vertex (my-values/infra/litellm-config.yaml:1–7), bounded Ops access (charts/ops-pod/templates/rbac.yaml:9–40,63–91), and monitoring observation (gitops/platform/values/alloy.yaml:30–45). These demonstrate declarations, not live availability or enforcement. Host → K3s remains an existing-platform prerequisite, not implemented host bootstrap. Flannel's dotted future alternative must remain explicitly unsupported; Argo and monitoring remain optional. Complete primary-contract proof for every remaining arrow, including K3s DNS/scheduler supply, was not established in this review; those edges are not awarded acceptance. No tests, generators, product execution, edits, nested reviews, broader diagram acceptance, or global gates were performed or awarded.
